parts.title: Part 1 — Introduction and interview
parts.instructions: Before the recorded interview begins, the examiner will check your identity by asking your full name and confirming your identification. This is not scored. The scored Part 1 then begins with general questions about yourself and a few familiar topics. Answer naturally and try to extend each answer with a reason or example. This part lasts 4–5 minutes.

questions.question: Let's talk about your work or studies. Do you work or are you a student?
What do you enjoy most about your work or studies?
Is there anything you would like to learn in the future?
Now let's talk about your free time. What do you usually do in your free time?
How often do you spend time with your friends?
What kind of music do you like?
Do you enjoy reading books? Why or why not?
Let's move on to your daily life. How often do you use public transport?
What is your favourite season of the year?
Do you prefer living in a city or the countryside? Why?

parts.title: Part 2 — Individual long turn
parts.instructions: You will be given a topic card. You have one minute to prepare and may make notes. Then speak for one to two minutes. Try to keep talking until the examiner stops you.
parts.cue_card_topic: Describe a memorable journey you have taken.
cue_card_bullets: and explain why this journey was memorable

questions.question: Would you like to take a similar journey again in the future?

parts.title: Part 3 — Two-way discussion
parts.instructions: The examiner will ask further questions connected to the Part 2 topic. These are more abstract and require you to explain, compare, and speculate. Try to give extended, well-reasoned answers. This part lasts 4–5 minutes.

questions.question: How has tourism changed over the last twenty years?
What are the advantages of domestic travel compared to travelling abroad?
Do you think technology has made travelling easier, or has it created new problems as well?
What impact does tourism have on local communities — do you think the benefits outweigh the drawbacks?
How do you think people will travel in the future?
